institutionName: Panteion University of Social and Political Sciences

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That my financial situation allowed it and that it was in southern Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Extremely hard. The educational system in Panteion and the structure was very different from Copenhagen. It was more or less within the first two weeks of my stay that I even had the opportunity to know the courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assisted by Erasmus+ student team.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Except from physical visits at the erasmus office, it has been extremely hard to keep in contact with the Panteion. Often mails would go unanswered or maybe take 2-3 weeks to get answered.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy in facebook groups, or maybe i was just lucky. But I made a post in an expat group and a woman contacted me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it differs a lot, and depends on which kind of university you travel to. For me living on campus wasn't an opportunity and since many of the locals still lived with they parents, I felt extremely lucky and independent to have a place on my own. But I think living on campus can also be a nice experience if that is what most students do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No housing available

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, extremely unstructured, uninformed and unorganised. Especially the OLA was so hard to get through since the courses were created last minute and thereby also made it hard to get the Erasmus grant.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before the first week we had to come to the erasmus office to fill out some papers. Then a few days later there was some digital introduction on zoom.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The erasmus office and the erasmus student team

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not succesfull. Only one of the antrhoplogy courses on the webside ended up being created, so I had to pick very random courses from the other departments. And apply for it around 5 times in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trust the proces, and know that probably something will be different from your initial wished, but it's gonna work out and people are only interested in getting you through the system.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Like I said above not very satisfied because almost none of the courses on the website was created.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that it is impossible to elaborate on the level, because the teaching style was so different from the danish one. It was more of a "gymnasium" style teaching, with a class and a teacher creating group work.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Not as much reading or structure.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of the internet (media and communication department)
English language for media and communication (media and communication department)
Key issues in psychology 1 (psychology department)
Systems theory & social media (psychology department)
History of psychology (psychology department)
Critical ethnographies of precariousness, precarity and care (anthropology department)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of the internet was definately the most structued one, but the professors on the department of anthropology also had some really exciting researches.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really, most stuff was super affordable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I knew that Greece would be cheap because of the financial crisis, but I was actually surprised about the supermarket prices and how similar they were to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Extremely nice expat opportunities both inside and outside school.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports clubs of different kinds. But I ended up joining an expat sport center for free called "Yoga and sports in athens".

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend doing volunteer word. Great opportunity to meet other expat and give something back to the city - I did volunteering in "Khora" which worked with food distribution to homeless people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do usual turist stuff - museums, go for a run in the national garden, sit in a coffe shop with a book, take your flatmates out to eat, go to the market on saturdays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy I would say. I had been on vacation a lot of times in greece and I love the more "village" vibe atmosphere and relaxed attitude.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be hard to encounter locals in the erasmus enviroment, but maybe try and not sit together with your international friends but force yourself to sit with some locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything, but the lack of structure in the univeristy system.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed attitude and the village atmosphere, where most people in the local neighbourhood noticed you and asked where you came from

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Everything is gonna work out and you're gonna get your degree, even if the system is completely different. They only wan't you go get through.
2. Take things one day at a time, you're gonna encounter different phases of homesickness and joy, but everything will pass.
3. Try not to call your friends too much, it can interrupt the experience and make you more homesick.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the erasmus office! They are extremely helpfull and much more easy to get a hold on physically then digitally.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Knowing that I can be on my own in a totally strange place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maintaining a relationship longdistance

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
